title: This Animal Eats Cobras and Survives the Bite (Here's How)

scenes.text: This animal eats cobras. And it survives the bite.
The honey badger. Up to a quarter of its diet is venomous snakes.
Cobra venom works by jamming the switch that keeps your lungs moving. You stop breathing.
The badger's switch is shaped differently. The venom can't lock on.
One was seen bitten in the face by a puff adder. Five hours later it was hunting snakes again.
Pigs, hedgehogs and mongooses evolved the same trick. The honey badger just does it with more attitude.

description:
Honey badgers eat cobras and puff adders, and they survive bites that would kill a person.
Up to a quarter of their diet is venomous snakes. Researchers at the University of Minnesota found mutations in the badger's nicotinic acetylcholine receptor, the muscle switch that cobra venom normally blocks, so the toxin can't bind properly. Hedgehogs, mongooses and pigs evolved the same resistance independently. A wildlife writer watched one badger bitten in the face by a puff adder go back to hunting snakes about five hours later.
Which animal would you give a superpower to? Comment below.
first_comment: Honey badger skin is so loose that when a lion grabs it, the badger can twist around inside its own skin and bite back. Honey badger or wolverine: who wins?
